_meta.schema: {category: {exemplars:[{title, teaches, setup, verdict_json, _provenance}], anti_patterns:[{name, rule, teaches}]}}
_meta.ownership: exemplars[] = Lane I1 (synthetic rewrites, Decision E). anti_patterns[] = Lane I2 (per-category named failure modes, I2.3). Rotation cron (I1.4) regenerates exemplars[] from feedback; leaves anti_patterns[] untouched.
_meta.depth: COMPACT (Option A, dossier §3-ratified + dispatcher-binding): exemplar verdict_json = winner_index, winner_declaration, winner_reason, key_tradeoff, value_context only. Abridged teaching blocks — model still emits the FULL :582-611 schema.
_meta.contamination_rule: Decision E: synthetic rewrites of the S1 45-id bias patterns — different brands, same structure; never verbatim gold pairs. Source-pattern id recorded in each _provenance for G6 ex-template reporting.
_meta.guardrail_C: Decision C: H2/H4/climate GCC claims qualitative only (no store counts, branch names, unsourced numbers).
_meta.label: Every exemplar setup carries EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.
_meta.token_budget: worst block 670 tok / +$0.00168 per call vs +$0.002 gate (scripts/audit_exemplar_token_cost.py)

exemplars.title: Running cost decides value at near-parity specs (H1)
exemplars.setup: Two entry mono laser printers compare closely on print speed and resolution, but one uses replacement toner that costs noticeably less per page and is easy to restock in Bahrain. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: About 40% lower cost-per-page on toner makes it cheaper to own over 2 years.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival prints slightly sharper first-page text and wakes faster from sleep.

value_context.product_0: At a near-identical purchase price, the lower running cost makes it the stronger value-per-dinar for a Bahrain home office.
value_context.product_1: A capable printer, but the dearer toner narrows its value once months of refills are counted.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H1 running-cost-decides-value at spec parity; generic printer framing distinct from the verbatim Epson/HP and Brother/Canon gold pairs.

exemplars.title: Compressor durability licenses the premium for long summers (H3)
exemplars.setup: Two 1.5-ton inverter ACs cool a room equally on paper, but the pricier one has a more reliable compressor and quieter operation that hold up through long Bahrain summers. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: More durable compressor justifies about 10% more for years of heavy summer cooling.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival AC costs less up front and matches the same 1.5-ton cooling capacity.

value_context.product_0: The premium is licensed by compressor reliability that matters under sustained Gulf heat, not just brand name.
value_context.product_1: Genuinely cheaper today, but a less proven compressor is a bigger risk over long summers.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H3 durability-justifies-premium; the H1/H3 electronics discriminator taught without a fixed direction. Climate marker kept qualitative per Decision C.

exemplars.title: Update guarantee and local warranty break a near-spec tie (H4)
exemplars.setup: A mid-range phone and a slightly cheaper rival land close on screen and chipset, but one carries more years of guaranteed OS updates and a wider Bahrain warranty network. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Around 2 extra years of guaranteed Android updates extend its useful life.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival phone is cheaper and matches it closely on day-one screen and camera specs.

value_context.product_0: The modest premium buys longer software support and easier local warranty service, which holds resale value.
value_context.product_1: Strong value on paper today, but a shorter update window shortens how long it stays current.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H4 local-service/update-guarantee breaks a spec tie; availability + warranty claims qualitative per Decision C (no store counts/branch names).

exemplars.title: Everyday value beats gift-tier pricing for daily use (H1)
exemplars.setup: A premium gift-tier date brand and a widely-sold everyday date brand are both good quality, but the everyday brand costs a fraction as much for the same daily snacking use. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Costs roughly 65% less per kilo for the same daily snacking quality.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The gift-tier brand has more refined presentation and stuffed-date variety for occasions.

value_context.product_0: Excellent value-per-dinar for daily eating, where freshness and price matter more than presentation.
value_context.product_1: Priced for gifting and special occasions, so it is a different purchase rather than a worse one.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H1 everyday-value-vs-gift-tier; generic date framing avoids the verbatim Al Foah/Bateel gold pair.

exemplars.title: Roast quality licenses a small premium (H3)
exemplars.setup: Two gold-label instant coffees sit one tier apart on price; the dearer one uses a smoother, less bitter roast that regular coffee drinkers notice cup after cup. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Smoother, less bitter roast justifies about 30% more per jar for daily drinkers.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The cheaper jar is perfectly drinkable and costs less for the same cup count.

value_context.product_0: Solid value for a no-fuss daily cup where roast nuance is not the priority.
value_context.product_1: The premium is licensed by a noticeably smoother roast you taste every morning, not just marketing.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H3 roast-quality-justifies-premium; the grocery H1/H3 disjoint pair (value-wins vs premium-wins).

exemplars.title: Regional staple wins on adoption (H2)
exemplars.setup: An imported Earl Grey and a regionally-beloved Earl Grey are close on tea quality; the regional brand has stronger bergamot and is the everyday favourite on Bahrain shelves. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Bolder bergamot and broad GCC adoption make it the everyday favourite at about 20% less.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The imported brand carries heritage prestige and a lighter, more delicate bergamot.

value_context.product_0: A respected import, priced for its name as much as the cup in the glass.
value_context.product_1: Strong value and the crowd-pleasing choice widely available across Bahrain.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H2 regional-staple-wins-on-adoption; GCC claims qualitative ('broad GCC adoption', 'widely available') per Decision C — no popularity numbers.

exemplars.title: Cost-per-gram decides daily supplementation (H1)
exemplars.setup: A bulk vitamin C in tablets and a single-serve sachet immune product deliver similar vitamin C, but the tablets cost far less per gram for daily use. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: About 75% lower cost per gram of vitamin C for daily use.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The sachets dissolve into a flavoured drink and add some B-vitamins and electrolytes.

value_context.product_0: Clear value-per-dinar for steady daily supplementation, where cost per gram is what compounds.
value_context.product_1: Convenient and pleasant, but you pay a premium per gram for the single-serve format.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H1 cost-per-gram value; format (tablets vs sachets) preserved, framing generalised away from verbatim brand claims.

exemplars.title: Better absorption licenses a small premium (H3)
exemplars.setup: Two turmeric curcumin supplements are close on curcumin content, but the dearer one adds a black-pepper extract that meaningfully improves absorption per serving. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Added piperine raises curcumin absorption up to 20x per serving.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The plain curcumin costs a little less per bottle for the same label curcumin.

value_context.product_0: Cheaper per bottle, but lower absorption can mean you effectively get less from each dose.
value_context.product_1: The premium is licensed by a real bioavailability gain, so more of what you pay for is actually used.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H3 absorption-justifies-premium; supplements has only 2 graded bias fails so the H1/H3 pair is the right two-exemplar set.

exemplars.title: Affordable dupe matches the prestige glow (H1)
exemplars.setup: A drugstore liquid-glow product gives a very similar lit-from-within finish to a prestige complexion filter that costs several times more. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Delivers a near-identical glow at roughly 65% less than the prestige filter.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The prestige filter has a finer shade range and a slightly more refined finish on close inspection.

value_context.product_0: Outstanding value-per-dinar: the glow effect most buyers want, for a fraction of the prestige cost.
value_context.product_1: A polished product, but you pay a prestige premium for a difference many will not notice day to day.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H1 dupe-matches-prestige-at-a-fraction; generic 'drugstore vs prestige' framing avoids the verbatim e.l.f./Charlotte Tilbury gold pair.

exemplars.title: Iconic shade and bulletproof wear license the premium (H3)
exemplars.setup: A prestige matte lipstick in an iconic shade outlasts a close drugstore matte through a full day of wear and transfers far less. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Holds a clean matte for about 8 hours with minimal transfer versus the drugstore fade.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The drugstore matte costs roughly half as much and covers the same everyday shade family.

value_context.product_0: Solid value for an everyday matte where all-day perfection is not essential.
value_context.product_1: The premium is licensed by genuinely longer, cleaner wear and an iconic shade payoff, not just the name.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H3 longevity/iconic-finish justifies premium; the H1/H3 makeup discriminator pair taught without a fixed direction.

exemplars.title: Humidity hold matters in the Gulf (H8)
exemplars.setup: Two drugstore setting powders are close on price and finish, but one keeps shine under control noticeably longer through humid Gulf days. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Controls shine well past 6 hours in humidity where the rival breaks down sooner.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival powder has a slightly softer, more natural finish for dry-skin days.

value_context.product_0: Strong value for the Gulf climate, where humidity longevity is what you are really paying for.
value_context.product_1: Good for drier conditions, but its shorter humid-day hold makes it a weaker match for summer here.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H8 climate (humidity hold) — the short, unambiguous Gulf-climate clause flagged ideal in dossier §2.

exemplars.title: Stronger resurfacing per dinar for experienced users (H1)
exemplars.setup: A potent weekly exfoliating treatment costs less per bottle than a gentler rival toner and delivers stronger resurfacing for users who already tolerate acids. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Higher acid concentration gives stronger resurfacing at roughly 30% less per bottle.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival toner is gentler for daily use and better suited to sensitive or beginner skin.

value_context.product_0: Excellent value-per-dinar for experienced users who want maximum resurfacing strength.
value_context.product_1: A milder daily option that justifies its price for sensitive skin, not for raw potency.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H1 potency-per-dinar for experienced users; generic acid-treatment framing, not the verbatim gold pair.

exemplars.title: Clinical gold standard licenses the premium (H3)
exemplars.setup: A higher-priced vitamin C serum is the clinically established, well-studied formulation, while a cheaper rival is good but less proven for stability and results. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Decades of stability and efficacy data back the formula despite costing about 2x more.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The cheaper serum offers a similar vitamin C percentage at a far friendlier price.

value_context.product_0: Strong value if you want effective vitamin C without paying for the heritage formulation.
value_context.product_1: The premium is licensed by a proven, stable, gold-standard formula many dermatologists trust.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H3/H6 gold-standard justifies premium; serum framing kept generic.

exemplars.title: Lighter finish suits daily high-UV Gulf wear (H8)
exemplars.setup: Two dermo-cosmetic SPF 50 sunscreens are matched on protection, but one has a lighter, less-greasy finish that wears better under daily Gulf sun and heat. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Same SPF 50 protection with a non-greasy finish that holds up in 40-plus heat.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival is a touch more moisturising, which drier skin may prefer in winter.

value_context.product_0: Strong value for daily high-UV Gulf wear, where a wearable lightweight finish drives reapplication.
value_context.product_1: Good protection too, but the heavier finish is a weaker fit for hot, humid daily use.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H8 climate (lighter finish for high-UV heat); SPF parity makes the climate-fit the deciding factor.

exemplars.title: Transparent formula at a fair price wins on value (H1)
exemplars.setup: A clearly-labelled peptide hair serum supports density at a fair price, while a rival oil treatment is pricier with less ingredient transparency. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Clear active labelling and targeted support at roughly 30% less than the rival.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival oil doubles as a scalp-and-skin multi-use product some prefer.

value_context.product_0: Strong value-per-dinar: transparent, targeted actives at a fair everyday price.
value_context.product_1: A pleasant multi-use oil, but you pay more for less clarity on what is actually working.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H1 transparency/value at fair price; generic serum-vs-oil framing.

exemplars.title: Faster visible repair licenses the premium (H3)
exemplars.setup: A premium leave-in peptide mask shows faster visible repair on damaged hair than a close, cheaper bond-builder rival. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Bioactive peptides show visible repair in about 1-2 uses, faster than the rival.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival bond-builder costs less and is a proven staple for gradual strengthening.

value_context.product_0: Good value for steady, gradual repair on a budget.
value_context.product_1: The premium is licensed by faster, more visible results for badly damaged hair.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H3 faster-results justifies premium; bond-builder framing kept generic.

exemplars.title: Lighter formula and wide availability win the everyday pick (H4)
exemplars.setup: Two coconut-based shampoos are close on cleansing, but one has a lighter everyday formula and is more widely available in Bahrain. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Lighter daily formula plus easy local restocking edge it for everyday use, at the same ~3 BHD price.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival is richer and more moisturising for very dry or curly hair.

value_context.product_0: Good value for dry hair that wants a richer wash.
value_context.product_1: Strong everyday value: a lighter formula that is widely available in Bahrain for easy repurchase.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H4 availability/everyday-fit; availability claim kept qualitative ('widely available in Bahrain') per Decision C.

exemplars.title: Value clone-tier projection wins on price (H1)
exemplars.setup: A value clone-tier designer-adjacent fragrance projects strongly and costs a fraction of the niche house it echoes, while the rival clone is close but pricier. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Strong projection at roughly 75% less than a comparable niche bottle.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival has a slightly smoother dry-down for those who notice the top-note sharpness.

value_context.product_0: Excellent value-per-dinar: niche-adjacent projection without the niche price.
value_context.product_1: Also good value, but the small refinement gain does not offset the higher price for most.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H1 clone-tier value-projection; generic 'value clone vs pricier clone' framing avoids the verbatim Armaf/Afnan pair.

exemplars.title: Niche longevity and sillage license the premium (H3)
exemplars.setup: A niche fragrance vastly outlasts a close designer rival in longevity and sillage, justifying its higher price for collectors. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Lasts about 10-12 hours with heavy sillage versus the designer's shorter wear.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The designer rival is far cheaper and more office-safe for daily wear.

value_context.product_0: Strong value for an everyday designer scent that performs well enough for work.
value_context.product_1: The premium is licensed by genuinely superior longevity and projection for special occasions.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H3 niche-longevity justifies premium; the H1/H3 fragrance discriminator pair.

exemplars.title: Viral GCC crowd-pleaser wins on broad appeal (H2)
exemplars.setup: A sweet-gourmand fragrance is the viral GCC crowd-pleaser with broad daily appeal, while a close rival is good but lacks the same regional pull. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Broad daily-wear appeal and crowd-pleasing profile at around 6 BHD make it the safe pick.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival is more distinctive for someone who wants to stand out rather than fit in.

value_context.product_0: Strong value and the GCC crowd-pleaser that suits the widest range of daily occasions.
value_context.product_1: A characterful alternative, priced similarly but with narrower everyday appeal.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H2 viral-GCC-crowd-pleaser; 'broad daily appeal'/'GCC crowd-pleaser' kept qualitative per Decision C (no popularity numbers).

exemplars.title: Better value and wider compatibility win (H1)
exemplars.setup: Two leather watch straps are close on look and quality, but one costs less and fits a wider range of watches. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Genuine leather and broader lug compatibility at roughly 30% less than the rival.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival strap carries a more recognisable fashion-brand name on the buckle.

value_context.product_0: A respected name, but you pay extra for the branding more than the leather.
value_context.product_1: Strong value-per-dinar: comparable leather, wider fit, lower price.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H1 value/compatibility; generic strap framing.

exemplars.title: Solar movement and ownership horizon license the premium (H3)
exemplars.setup: A solar-powered analogue watch needs no charging or battery swaps, making it a more durable long-term timepiece than a feature-rich smartwatch that ages faster. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Solar movement runs for years with no charging, outlasting a smartwatch's 2-3 year horizon.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The smartwatch offers notifications and fitness tracking the analogue cannot.

value_context.product_0: Good value if you want smart features now and accept a shorter useful life.
value_context.product_1: The premium is licensed by a decade-plus ownership horizon with no battery upkeep.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H3/H7 durability-ownership-horizon justifies premium; the H1/H3 fashion discriminator pair.

exemplars.title: Benchmark durability holds value despite the premium (H4)
exemplars.setup: An iconic denim jean is the benchmark for durable, consistent fit and is easy to find and replace, justifying a premium over a cheaper rival. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Durable iconic denim and consistent fit hold up for years despite costing about 30% more.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival jean fits similarly and costs noticeably less up front.

value_context.product_0: The premium is licensed by benchmark durability and a fit you can reliably re-buy.
value_context.product_1: Genuinely cheaper and a fair everyday jean, with less of a track record for longevity.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H4/H6 benchmark-durability + easy-rebuy; framing kept generic, availability qualitative.

exemplars.title: Larger tank and local service at a lower price win (H1)
exemplars.setup: Two evaporative air coolers are close on cooling, but one has a larger water tank and local service support at a lower price for the Gulf's dry-heat needs. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Bigger tank runs longer between refills and costs about 15% less than the rival.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival cooler is a little more compact and quieter on its lowest setting.

value_context.product_0: A tidy compact cooler, but the smaller tank and higher price weaken its value here.
value_context.product_1: Strong value-per-dinar for Gulf dry-heat cooling, with longer runtime and local service backing.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H1+H8 value at lower price for dry-heat; service claim kept qualitative per Decision C.

exemplars.title: Proven reliability over a long service life licenses the premium (H3)
exemplars.setup: A premium water heater with a corrosion-resistant tank and proven reliability justifies its price for long Bahrain service life over a cheaper rival. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Corrosion-resistant tank and proven reliability add 3-5 years of service life over the rival.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The cheaper heater costs less today and matches the same tank capacity.

value_context.product_0: The premium is licensed by longer service life against hard water, not just brand name.
value_context.product_1: Cheaper now, but a shorter expected lifespan erodes the saving over a full ownership cycle.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H3 reliability-justifies-premium; distinct framing from the electronics water-heater exemplar (this one leads on the reliability/heritage angle, that one on the ownership-cost math).

exemplars.title: Local pod availability and brew quality win the everyday pick (H4)
exemplars.setup: Two pod coffee machines are close on price, but one has easier pod availability in the Bahrain market and better brew quality for daily use. EXAMPLE — abridged, do not copy structure or content.

verdict_json.winner_reason: Easier local pod restocking and richer brew win the daily pick within 5 BHD of the rival.
verdict_json.key_tradeoff: The rival machine is more compact and its pods can be a touch cheaper online.

value_context.product_0: Strong everyday value: brew quality plus pods that are easy to buy in Bahrain.
value_context.product_1: Compact and capable, but thinner local pod availability makes daily restocking harder.

_provenance.rewrite_note: H4 pod-availability/everyday-fit; availability kept qualitative per Decision C.
